articles.summary: On Veterans Day, we celebrate the willingness of those who have served and are serving to sacrifice for our country.

articles.title_zh: 战场之外：退伍军人自杀与生命价值
articles.content: “We’ll teach you how to kill. When you get back, you’re the VA’s problem.” That’s what they told my old team sergeant before he deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division. The risk of killing or being killed is an inescapable part of military service. In the Army, recruits go through a formation process in Basic Combat Training that turns them into soldiers. Part of this means learning that the mission always comes first, which in turn must mean they’re expendable. First aid is taught with the assumption that at some point, someone will need a tourniquet, chest seal, or body bag. After all, the enemy also learns to shoot, and sometimes the mission requires soldiers to get into harm’s way. That’s part of the tragic necessity of war. No one would have followed Washington across the Delaware or left the landing craft on D-Day if staying alive were the number-one goal. A commander’s ability to orchestrate force in combat would break down with a military unwilling to die. But this same dynamic that makes militaries potent threatens the lives of those who fight, through the tragedy of veteran suicide. Necessity of Sacrifice We must understand sacrifice as more than mere operational necessity: Something is lost when nothing is worth dying for. C. S. Lewis famously warned of the danger of making men without chests—of a people without an anchoring morality to mediate the carnal passions of the stomach and the cold calculations of the head. A society full of people consumed with their own survival doesn’t bode well for its moral character, to say nothing of its national defense. Americans ought to be thankful that thousands of young men and women regularly sign the dotted line to join the armed forces, volunteering to put their country’s well-being ahead of their own. A society full of people consumed with their own survival doesn’t bode well for its moral character. The willingness to sacrifice that makes a military effective can carry a hidden cost. What happens when a soldier learns to put his life second, then struggles to understand its value when the mission ends? A soldier who was prepared to take a bullet downrange may think little of a bottle of whiskey, a pack of cigarettes, or opening up his motorcycle on the highway. When the Mission Ends Those who make it back from combat alive aren’t entirely safe. Veterans take their own lives at roughly twice the rate of the general population. Veteran suicide stems from a number of factors, including post-traumatic stress, moral injury, difficulty transitioning to civilian life, loss of purpose and social connection, traumatic brain injury, pain, and proximity to firearms. Alongside these factors, we should consider what it means to spend years learning to put one’s life second and what happens when that lesson outlasts the mission. There’s an obvious tension when it comes to the value of life. Christians know that our lives in this world aren’t ultimate (Rev. 12:11). Christians can face death because we recognize this life’s limits, while still treating life as a gift worthy of protection. As Jesus taught, being willing to die for others is the highest form of love (John 15:13). This is why the second person of the Trinity stepped down from heaven, took on the form of a servant, and obediently followed the Father’s mission orders to death on the cross (Phil. 2:6–8). Yet Jesus didn’t throw his life away; he demonstrated perfect courage. Between the foolhardiness that leads to blood on the highway and the cowardice that keeps men in hiding when a wolf growls at the door, stands courage. As G. K. Chesterton observes, “Courage is almost a contradiction in terms. It means a strong desire to live taking the form of a readiness to die.” We see this in Christ’s agony in anticipation of the cross in the garden of Gethsemane (Luke 22:44). Yet he carried his cross anyway. Value of Life and Virtue of Sacrifice The Christian worldview ties together the value of both life and sacrifice,

articles.content: A wave of viral social media videos featuring Malaysian citizens publicly declaring their departure from state-sanctioned Sunni Islam has cast a harsh spotlight on the severe lack of religious freedom in the Southeast Asian nation. While state authorities have scrambled to investigate and suppress the footage, international religious freedom advocates warn that the phenomenon highlights a much deeper, systemic crisis: the complete criminalization of apostasy for ethnic Malays and the intense persecution faced by those who desire to follow other faiths, including Christianity. Under Article 160 of the Constitution of Malaysia, all ethnic Malays are legally defined as Muslims. This constitutional binding leaves no legal avenue for a Malay individual to officially change their religion. For those who experience a personal crisis of faith or choose to embrace Christianity, the path forward is fraught with state-sponsored surveillance, social ostracism, and severe legal penalties. Central to this machinery of suppression is the powerful federal agency JAKIM (Department of Islamic Development Malaysia) and state-level enforcers like JAIS (Selangor Islamic Religious Department). Together, they operate a rigid, dual-track legal system where Shariah courts hold near-absolute jurisdiction over Muslims. Requests by individuals to officially exit Islam are systematically rejected. Instead of granting freedom of conscience, JAIS and other state bodies actively weaponize mandatory detention in state-run Islamic rehabilitation centers (pusat pemurnian akidah). These centers function as forced re-education camps. Converts who are caught or who attempt to petition the courts for apostasy are routinely sentenced to months of involuntary confinement. Inside, they are subjected to intense psychological pressure, isolation, and compulsory doctrinal lectures designed to break their resolve and force a recantation. Recently, JAIS publicized a court-ordered Istitabah (forced repentance ritual) for a social media figure, signaling that the state will use its full administrative weight to enforce religious compliance. Recent landmark legal battles from 2025 and 2026 expose a devastating reality: born-Muslims face a structural wall of total rejections. In an Oct. 2, 2025 ruling, the Federal Court — Malaysia’s highest civil judiciary — completely shut down a final appeal from a 47-year-old Christian convert who spent years fighting the Shariah court system just to return to his original faith following a divorce. The apex court reaffirmed that civil courts have zero jurisdiction to override Shariah rejections, leaving the believer legally trapped. Similarly, on Jan. 6, 2025, a Selangor woman who was unilaterally converted to Islam as a child saw her final legal challenge collapse at the Federal Court, cementing the precedent that her state identity card (MyKad) must permanently brand her as a Muslim. Even elderly believers who have secretly practiced their faith for decades are being hunted through bureaucracy. In June 2026, a 58-year-old mother filed a prominent judicial review against the National Registration Department (JPN) after they flatly refused to remove the “Islam” label from her identification card — despite her having formally converted out of Islam via a deed poll more than 30 years ago. JPN continues to trap her under state custody, demanding a clearance letter from the Shariah court that officials refuse to grant. The statistics highlight how tightly the trap is wound. Historical data shows that out of 863 formal applications submitted nationwide to leave Islam during a 10-year period, only 168 were granted. Legal analysts emphasize that nearly 100% of those rare exceptions were administrative clerical corrections in East Malaysia — such as a Jan. 7 Kota Kinabalu High Court ruling where a father and three children successfully proved they were raised Christian and that an NRD officer had made a data-entry error. articles.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! articles.content: The following is the substance of a pamphlet published by Archibald G. Brown, a student and then great ally of C. H. Spurgeon in the cause of the gospel in London. Brown here draws attention to a practice that was gaining ground in the churches of his day: that of holding ‘amusements’ of various kinds, which obscured, diverted from, and in some cases replaced the proper ministry of local churches. Brown was savagely attacked in the wake of the publication of the pamphlet, derided as ‘a kill-joy,’ ‘a morbid pietist,’ and ‘a sour bigot.’ His meaning, however, had been deliberately misrepresented. 1 Brown nowhere objects to all amusement per se , but amusement which masquerades as ministry, distracting the church and deceiving needy sinners. While the context in which Brown wrote may be different from ours, we need to hear his burden for a Church—and for Christians—to make a decisive break with the world and its practices. An Evil in the Camp of the Lord DIFFERENT days demand their own special testimony. The watchman who would be faithful to his Lord and the City of his God has need to carefully note the signs of the times and emphasize his witness accordingly. Con­cerning the testimony needed now, there can the little, if any, doubt. An evil is in the professed camp of the Lord—so gross, so brazen in its impudence—that the most short-sighted of spiritual men can hardly fail to notice it. During the past few years it has developed at an ab­normal rate, ever for evil. It has worked like leaven until now the whole lump ferments. Look which way you may, its presence makes itself manifest. There is little if any­thing, to choose between Church, Chapel, or Mission Hall. However they may differ in some respects, they bear a striking likeness in the posters that figure upon and dis­figure their notice boards. Amusement for the people i s the leading article advertised by each. If any of my readers doubt my statement, or think my utterance too sweeping, let them take a tour of inspection and study “the announce­ments for the week” at the doors of the sanctuaries of the neighbourhood; or let them read the religious advertise­ments in their local papers. I have done this again and again, until the hideous fact has been proved up to the hilt, that “amusement” is ousting the preaching of the gospel as the great attraction: “Concerts,” “Entertain­ments,” “Fancy Fairs,” “Smoking Conferences,” “Dramatic Performances,” are the words honoured with biggest type and most startling colours. articles.title_zh: 俄亥俄州派遣庆祝活动确认33名IMB传教士为全球服务
articles.content: Participants at the IMB Sending Celebration on Nov. 9, 2026, celebrated God's faithfulness in sending 33 new missionaries to the nations. Held at the Sugarcreek campus of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, the event launched the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio annual gathering. For security reasons, some newly appointed missionaries are not publicly identified. IMB Photo God continues to call His people to carry the gospel to the ends of the earth. During a Sending Celebration Nov. 9 at the Sugarcreek Campus of First Baptist Church Kettering, near Dayton, Ohio, 33 International Mission Board missionaries stood before family, friends and supporters, affirming their obedience to that call. Trustees of the IMB appointed the fully supported missionaries who represent 10 states – including two candidates from Ohio – and many Southern Baptist churches committed to sending and sustaining those called by God to go to the mission field. Senior Pastor Chad Keck welcomed those in attendance, sharing his appreciation for the partnership with Southern Baptist churches to cooperatively send and support missionaries. The Sending Celebration is meeting in conjunction with the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio. Chad Keck, senior pastor of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, left, and Jeremy Westbrook, executive director-treasurer of the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio, right, welcome guests gathered for the IMB Sending Celebration, which kicked off the convention’s annual gathering. IMB Photo Among those who shared their stories include a couple who answered an unexpected call later in life, a couple who are returning to Albania and to people they could not forget; and a couple who moved from welcoming the nations in Canada to going to Fiji. All of them shared their stories before the Sending Celebration. Unexpected invitation to go On Dec. 5, 2025, what seemed like an ordinary FaceTime call became a turning point for Rob Boss. As he spoke with his daughter, Hannah, during her IMB training, Rob sensed God speaking clearly to his heart: “You can do this too.” The impression was unexpected. After decades of writing, Christian education, seminary teaching and active support of missions, overseas service had never been part of Rob and Stephanie Boss’ plans. “It wasn’t an audible voice, but it was so clear,” Rob said. “It was Him. It was so kind and so gentle and so encouraging.” The moment drove him to his knees in surrender. When Stephanie came home later that day, he told her he believed God was calling them to the nations. Her response was immediate. “Thrilled is the right answer,” she said. The next day, the couple contacted the IMB and began the application process. Though missions had long been part of their family’s story, Rob and Stephanie Boss sensed God leading them to overseas service while encouraging their daughter, Hannah, during her missionary training. Sent by Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, Texas, they are now headed to Colombia, where they will serve through theological education. IMB Photo Looking back, the Bosses see the Lord’s hand preparing them long before they realized where He was leading. “God brought us together in the summer of 1990 at Glorieta, New Mexico, where we met and married,” Stephanie said during the Sending Celebration. What followed was years of ministry, teaching, parenting and navigating life’s unexpected turns, which taught them to hold plans loosely and trust God completely. “We did not have a clue about what life held in front of us,” Stephanie said. “We just knew we wanted to follow the Lord.” Their calling also continues a family legacy. Rob’s mother served with the IMB in Africa after retirement, helping inspire Hannah’s service in South Korea. Now, three generations of the same family have answered God’s call to the nations. Rob and Stephanie expressed deep gratitude for their sending church, Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, whose strong commitment to missions
articles.content_zh:
2026年11月9日的IMB送信庆典的参与者,庆祝上帝向各国派遣33名新传教士的忠诚. 该活动在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling的Sugarcreek校园举行,在俄亥俄州发起了浸信会州议会年会。 出于安全考虑,一些新任命的传教士没有公开身份.

在分享自己故事的人中,有一对夫妇在生活后期意外地接了电话,一对夫妇正在返回阿尔巴尼亚,一对夫妇无法忘记;一对夫妇从欢迎加拿大各国搬到斐济。 他们都分享了他们的故事 在送信庆典之前。 意外邀请 Dec 上。

5, 2025, 看起来像一个普通的FaceTime电话成为Rob Boss的转折点. 当他和他的女儿汉娜在IMB训练期间交谈时,罗布感应到上帝对他说的很清楚:“你也可以这样做。” 印象出乎意料。

接下来是多年的教职、教职、养育和过着意想不到的转折,教他们松动计划,完全相信上帝。 Stephanie说:“我们不知道我们面前的生活是什么。” 我们只知道我们想跟随主。 他们的召唤也延续了家庭遗产。

罗布的母亲退休后在非洲为IMB效力,帮助激励汉娜在韩国服役. 现在,同一家庭的三代人响应了上帝向各国发出的呼吁。 Rob和Stephanie深表感谢他们派来的教会Worth堡的Wedgwood浸信会教堂,他们坚定致力于使命

articles.title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
articles.summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
articles.summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
articles.title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
articles.content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
articles.content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

articles.title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
articles.summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
articles.summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
articles.title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
articles.content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.

articles.title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
articles.title_zh: 他们把牧师关进了精神病病房。他带领一百人归向耶稣
articles.content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.

他走了出去 埋下了好消息 在最后的地方 没有人会寻找它。 上帝不会被任何锁住你的门锁住 他已经在里面等了

articles.title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
articles.content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .

查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

articles.content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. articles.title_zh: 犹太难民成为副牧师
articles.content: Werner Simonson By Charles Gardner — At a time when Hitler aimed to harm us, here was a German who came to bless us! Holocaust survivor Werner Simonson escaped from Germany just before the outbreak of World War II, only to become a Church of England vicar. Of Jewish heritage, he was sacked as a judge by the Nazis and had to endure long years of separation from his non-Jewish wife and son before being reunited after the war. Like John Wesley who was rescued as a child from a rectory fire, Werner was also ‘a brand plucked from the burning’. He was about to be executed in a World War I battle with France when he and his colleagues were wrongly accused of shooting French prisoners. But just in time, one of the latter told the firing squad how Werner had treated him with kindness, even sharing his rations with him. The German soldier was thus spared but spent the next five years as a prisoner of the French, his POW status only ending in 1920 after being put to work restoring war damage in northern France. When finally released, it was a case of ‘from the frying pan into the fire’ as Germany was plunged into despair and division following their ignominious defeat. Despite this, however, Werner quickly rose to the status of high court judge before being dismissed from his post by the Nazis when they discovered his Jewish heritage. The fact that he had fought for Germany and had won the coveted Iron Cross for gallantry counted for nothing. And the increasing pressure of anticipating arrest led to a breakdown of his health. But while attending his niece’s confirmation at a Lutheran church, feeling at the end of his rope, it was as if the preacher was speaking directly into his desperate situation. He opened his heart to Christ and found new life and hope. “In the utter darkness which had engulfed my life I saw a new light,” he recalled.(1) He became associated with the Confessing Church opposing the Nazis’ antisemitic policies and was advised to escape which he managed to do with the help of the Bishop of Chichester Dr George Bell. Werner’s wife Leonie and son Juergen stayed behind but were able to join him after the war. Being German, he was initially interned with others on the Isle of Man where he led fellow Jews to faith in Christ. But tragic news followed, hearing of his father’s death, his mother being murdered in a concentration camp and his sister Ilse gassed in Auschwitz. Werner knew little English when he arrived on these shores but attracted much interest by being ordained at St Paul’s Cathedral when Britain was in the middle of a war with his fatherland. He was subsequently offered back the post of judge in the new West Germany along with a pension for the job from which he had been previously dismissed by the Nazis. But he turned down the generous offer. “I could not exchange service in the ministry of God for service in administering man-made law; accepting this offer would have meant abandoning God’s call to me, and this I could not do.” But this humble and self-effacing man was to make a significant impact in succeeding years as he proclaimed the gospel in three separate London parishes, ending up at St Luke’s, Hampstead, where (from 1956-1965) he helped yet more Jewish people to a knowledge of their Messiah. He continued passionately preaching Christ almost till his final breath in 1991, aged 101. 1 With grateful thanks to War and Grace by Don Stephens (Evangelical Press 2005), an imprint of 10Publishing. 维纳·西蒙森 查尔斯·加德纳 当希特勒想伤害我们的时候 有个德国人来祝福我们! 大屠杀幸存者维尔纳·西蒙森(Werner Simonson)在二战爆发前刚从德国逃出,只是成为英国牧师教堂.

由于犹太人的遗产,他被纳粹解雇为法官,不得不忍受与他非犹太妻子和儿子多年的分离,战争结束后才重新团聚. 就像小时候被救出来的约翰·卫斯理(John Wesley),

他在第一次世界大战与法国的战斗中即将被处决,当时他和他的同事被错误地指责射杀法国囚犯. 但就在时间上,后者之一告诉行刑队,沃纳如何以善意对待他,甚至与他分享他的口粮.

德国士兵因此幸免于难,但作为法国人的俘虏度过了接下来的五年,他的战俘身份直到1920年在法国北部被投入恢复战争破坏后才结束. 当德国在惨败之后陷入绝望和分裂。

尽管如此,维尔纳在发现他的犹太遗产后很快升格为高等法院法官,然后被纳粹解职. 他为德国而战 赢得了贪婪的铁十字勋章 他的英勇无足轻重 而预期被捕的压力越来越大,导致他的健康崩溃。

但当在路德会教堂出席侄女的确认仪式时,感觉他的绳索尽头,就像传教士直接谈到他的绝望处境一样. 他向基督敞开了心扉,找到了新的生命和希望.

" 在席卷我的生活的完全黑暗中,我看到了新的光芒, " 他回忆说。 (1) 他与反对纳粹反帝政策的忏悔教会有关联,并被劝告在奇切斯特主教乔治·贝尔博士的帮助下逃离。 维尔纳的妻子莱昂尼(Leonie)和儿子朱尔根(Juergen)留下,但战后得以加入他.

作为德国人,他最初在马恩岛和其他人一起被关押,在那里他带领犹太人同胞信仰基督. 但悲剧性的消息接踵而至,听到他父亲的死讯,他的母亲在集中营被谋杀,他的妹妹伊尔塞在奥斯威辛被毒气冲昏.

Werner在到达这些海岸时不懂英语, 随后他又被重新聘回新西德的法官职位,并同时获得先前被纳粹开除的职务养老金. 但他拒绝了慷慨的提议.

“我不能在上帝部交换服务,以服务于管理人造法律;

接受这个提议将意味着放弃上帝对我的召唤,我不能这样做。 但是,这位谦卑而自卑的人在接下来的岁月里,当他在三个独立的伦敦教区宣布福音时,将产生显著的影响,最后在汉普斯特德的圣卢克(St Luke),他在那里(从1956年到1965年)帮助了更多的犹太人民了解他们的弥赛亚。

他继续热情地宣扬基督,几乎到1991年他最后一口气为止,101. 1岁,感谢战争与恩典,唐·斯蒂芬斯著(福音出版社,2005年),10Publishing的印记. 犹太难民成为牧师,

articles.title_zh: 因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩
articles.content: On Nov. 6, an 18-year-old Christian girl named Ajak Mabior was beaten to death in Jonglei, South Sudan, after refusing to enter a forced marriage arranged by her family. She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it. After attempting to escape, she was killed by her own brother and cousin. Days later, police in Bor arrested the two men but released them without charges after family members demanded their freedom, arguing that “there was no case” because they were relatives. A Common Problem The killing has raised serious concerns among Christian leaders about the pressure Christian girls face when their faith and personal convictions conflict with family expectations. “When a young girl is killed for refusing a forced marriage, and the killers walk free because they are family, the message is clear: Tradition is stronger than the law, and stronger than the value of a life,” a local pastor said. “Many of our Christian daughters live under this same shadow.” For Christian girls in South Sudan , forced marriages can become a matter of religious persecution when they are pressured to marry outside their faith and abandon their Christian convictions. Those who refuse may face rejection, threats, intimidation, and violence from their own families. Mabior’s death highlights the vulnerability of young Christian women who seek to remain faithful to Christ while facing pressure to submit to marriages that violate their faith and conscience. “The church teaches that every life is precious because it is created in the image of God,” the pastor added. “Yet when a Christian girl refuses a marriage that would bind her against her will, she can be treated as a traitor to the community. We have buried too many who paid that price.” Seeking Justice The authorities’ response has added to the church’s concerns. Police reportedly released the suspects without the consent of the Jonglei State Caretaker Commissioner. The justification that the suspects were relatives raises serious questions about the protection available to Christian girls facing forced marriages and violence. When perpetrators are released without facing justice, vulnerable Christian women are left with little confidence that the authorities will protect their right to practice their faith and make decisions according to their conscience. “We preach freedom in Christ, but our young people still live in fear of the consequences of that freedom,” the pastor said. “If the police and local authorities remain quiet, the church becomes the only place left where these girls and boys can find a voice. We need courage to speak, and we need the wider Body of Christ to stand with us.” Mabior’s case raises concerns about forced interfaith marriages, religious pressure, and violence against young Christian women in South Sudan. “We call on the wider Body of Christ to pray for Ajak’s justice, and for the protection of Christian girls facing forced marriages because of their faith,” an International Christian Concern (ICC) staffer said. “Pray that the church will have the courage to speak against religious coercion and violence, and that the authorities will uphold the law and protect vulnerable believers.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . 11月6日,一名名叫Ajak Mabior的18岁基督教女孩在南苏丹琼格莱州因拒绝参加家庭安排的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。 她被期望嫁给一个年长的穆斯林男子——她反对这种婚姻,因为她的基督教信仰以及她不愿意被迫加入. 在试图逃跑后,她被自己的哥哥和表妹杀死.

几天后,Bor的警察逮捕了这两名男子,但在家属要求他们自由后,在没有指控的情况下将他们释放,他们辩称“没有案件”,因为他们是亲属。 常见问题 杀害事件引起了基督教领袖的严重关切,基督教女孩在信仰和个人信念与家庭期望相冲突时面临压力。

“当一名年轻女孩因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害,而杀人者因是家人而自由行动时,信息是明确的:传统比法律更强大,比生命的价值更强大。” 一位当地牧师说。

“我们许多基督教女儿生活在这种阴影下。” 对于南苏丹的基督教女孩来说,当她们被迫在信仰之外结婚并放弃基督教信仰时,强迫婚姻就可能成为宗教迫害的问题。 拒绝者可能面临自己家庭的排斥、威胁、恐吓和暴力。

Mabior的死亡凸显了基督教青年妇女的脆弱性,她们试图保持对基督的忠诚,同时面临压力,迫使她们向违反其信仰和良心的婚姻屈服。 牧师补充说,“教会教导每一条生命都是宝贵的,因为它是以上帝的形象创造的。”

“当一个基督教女孩拒绝违背她意愿而束缚她的婚姻时,她可以被当作一个叛徒对待。 我们埋葬了太多付出这一代价的人。” 寻求正义 当局的反应增加了教会的关注。 据报告,警方未经琼格莱州看守专员同意释放了嫌疑人。

关于嫌疑人是亲属的理由,令人对面临强迫婚姻和暴力的基督教女孩获得的保护提出严重问题。 当肇事者在没有受到法律制裁的情况下被释放时,脆弱的基督教妇女对当局将保护其信仰和根据其良心作出决定的权利缺乏信心。

牧师说,“我们在基督中宣扬自由,但我们的年轻人仍然生活在对这种自由的后果的恐惧之中。” “如果警察和地方当局保持安静,教堂就成了这些女孩和男孩能够发表意见的唯一地方。

我们需要勇气说话,我们需要更广泛的基督与我们站在一起。” Mabior案引起了人们对南苏丹境内强迫不同信仰间婚姻、宗教压力以及针对基督教青年妇女的暴力的关注。

“我们呼吁广大的基督机构为阿贾克的正义祈祷,并保护因信仰而面临强迫婚姻的基督教女孩。” 一位国际基督教关注组织的工作人员说。

“祈祷教会有勇气反对宗教胁迫和暴力,并祈祷当局将维护法律,保护脆弱的信徒。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

articles.title_zh: 马来西亚法院将一名皈依基督教者的宗教自由诉讼移交地区法庭
articles.content: A 34-year-old law graduate’s multi-year battle exposes the severe reality of religious control and the legal trap facing citizens who want to leave Islam. A high-stakes constitutional challenge highlighting the erosion of religious freedom in Malaysia has taken a procedural step backward. The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ordered that a lawsuit filed by a 34-year-old legal researcher seeking legal recognition as a Christian be transferred to the Shah Alam High Court. The case lays bare the rigid and intrusive control exercised by state apparatuses and Islamic religious authorities over personal faith, showcasing a system where basic human rights — such as choosing one’s own religion — are tightly policed by the government. A Life Labeled Without Consent The plaintiff, Shameer PV, identifies as a Christian and has lived as one since he was 18. However, under strict Malaysian administrative regulations, the word “Islam” was stamped on his compulsory national identity card (MyKad) when he was just 12, following a bureaucratic policy introduced under the National Registration Act. Despite decades of personal conviction and his marriage to a Christian wife, the state continues to legally treat him as a Muslim, directly violating his parental and marital status and refusing to recognize his family. Shameer’s legal challenge names the federal government, the Selangor state government, and the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) as defendants. He argues that labeling citizens by religion on state identity cards violates Article 11(1) of the Federal Constitution, which ostensibly guarantees every person the right to profess and practice their religion. Trapped in Shariah Bureaucracy Shameer’s ordeal underscores the labyrinthine and punishing hurdles forced upon religious minorities and converts in Malaysia’s dual-justice system, which runs a parallel set of Islamic (Shariah) courts alongside the civil judiciary. In 2018, Shameer initiated proceedings in a Selangor Shariah court seeking official recognition of his Christian faith. After an exhausting 72 court sessions spanning over seven years, the Shariah court dismissed his application in January. Rather than allowing him to move on with his life, the religious court went a step further, ordering state departments and Islamic authorities to “guide and control” his practice of Islam — effectively treating his desire to leave the faith as a disciplinary or correctional matter. Having exhausted the religious tribunal system, Shameer turned to the civil high court in July, filing an originating summons to ask the highest judicial authorities whether state-mandated religious labeling on identity cards is unconstitutional, and whether Shariah courts have any lawful jurisdiction over individuals who do not practice Islam. A Wider Crisis for Freedom of Conscience International human rights observers and religious freedom advocates have long criticized Malaysia’s legal framework regarding apostasy and conversion. While the Malaysian Constitution theoretically protects freedom of religion, civil courts have repeatedly ruled that only Islamic Shariah courts have the authority to permit someone to leave Islam — creating an effective judicial catch-22, as Shariah courts rarely grant permission to renounce the religion. For international human rights advocates and supporters of religious liberty, Shameer’s case is a stark reminder of the state-enforced religious controls facing millions in Southeast Asia. As his case moves to the Shah Alam court, the legal battle continues to test whether Malaysia’s secular constitutional framework can protect an individual’s fundamental right of conscience against a totalizing state religious bureaucracy. 一个34岁的法学毕业生的多年战斗暴露了宗教控制的严重现实和想要离开伊斯兰教的公民所面临的法律陷阱. 马来西亚宗教自由受到侵蚀,

吉隆坡高等法院下令将34岁法律研究者提出的寻求法律承认为基督徒的诉讼移交沙阿拉姆高等法院.

这一案件暴露了国家机构和伊斯兰宗教当局对个人信仰的严格和侵扰性控制,表明政府严格控制基本人权(如选择自己的宗教)的制度。 未经同意的生活标签 原告Shameer PV确认为基督教徒,自18岁起就一直作为一个教徒生活在一起。

然而,根据严格的马来西亚行政条例,他12岁时的强制性国民身份证(MyKad)上印有“伊斯兰”一词,这是根据《国家登记法》实行的官僚政策。

尽管几十年的个人信念和他与基督教妻子的婚姻,但国家继续在法律上将他视为穆斯林,直接侵犯了他的父母和婚姻状况,并拒绝承认他的家人. 沙门的法律质疑将联邦政府,雪兰莪州政府,雪兰莪伊斯兰宗教委员会(MAIS)列为被告.

他辩称,以宗教方式将公民贴在州身份证上违反了《联邦宪法》第11(1)条,该条表面上保障每个人信奉和奉行其宗教的权利。

伊斯兰教法官僚沙姆耶的折磨凸显了Labyrinthine和惩罚强加给宗教少数派和皈依马来西亚双重司法制度的障碍,马来西亚的双重司法制度与民事司法平行设有一套伊斯兰(伊斯兰教法)法院。 2018年,沙姆耶在塞兰哥教法法院提起诉讼,寻求官方承认他的基督教信仰.

经过历时七年的72次开庭,教法法院于1月驳回了他的申请。

宗教法庭没有让他继续自己的生活,而是更进一步,命令国家部门和伊斯兰当局“指导和控制”他的伊斯兰教习俗——实际上将他放弃信仰的愿望视为纪律或惩戒事项。

在用尽了宗教法庭制度之后,Shameer于7月向民事高等法院提交了原传票,询问最高司法当局在身份证上贴上国家规定的宗教标签是否违宪,伊斯兰教法法院是否对不信奉伊斯兰教的个人拥有任何合法管辖权。

国际人权观察员和宗教自由倡导者长期批评马来西亚关于叛教和皈依的法律框架。

虽然马来西亚宪法理论上保护宗教自由,但民事法院一再裁定只有伊斯兰教法法院有权允许某人离开伊斯兰教——这创造了有效的司法抓捕-22,因为伊斯兰教法法院很少允许放弃该宗教.

对国际人权倡导者和宗教自由支持者来说,Shameer一案明确提醒人们注意东南亚数百万人所面临的国家强制宗教控制。

articles.content:
콩고민주공화국 동부에서 이슬람국가(IS)와 연계된 무장단체에 납치돼 4년 넘게 억류됐던 기독교 여성이 우간다군에 의해 구출됐다. 그는 억류 기간 성폭력을 당하고 이슬람으로 개종하도록 강요받았지만, 내면의 신앙을 지켰다고 증언했다.

크리스천데일리인터내셔널(CDI)에 따르면, 국제기독교박해감시단체(ICC)는 최근 발표한 보고서에서 “2022년 7월 콩고민주공화국 동부 루메(Lume) 마을에서 납치된 카퉁구 음바카 다르케(Katungu Mbaka Darke)가 이투리주에서 우간다 인민방위군에 의해 구출됐다”고 밝혔다.

당시 오후 9시께 연합민주군(ADF) 대원들이 마을을 공격했고, 다르케는 이 과정에서 납치됐다. ADF는 콩고민주공화국 동부에서 활동하는 무장단체로, 이슬람국가(IS)와 연계돼 있다.

다르케는 억류 기간 성폭력과 종교적 강압을 겪었다. 그는 ICC에 전한 증언에서 “납치됐을 때 저는 아직 어렸다. 그들 중 한 명이 저에게 성관계를 강요했다. 이슬람을 받아들이고 꾸란 구절을 외우도록 강요하기도 했다. 겉으로는 받아들였지만 마음속으로는 예수님이 하나님이라는 사실을 알고 있었다”고 밝혔다.

그는 억류 기간 ADF 대원과의 사이에서 두 자녀를 낳은 것으로 전해졌다. 오랜 기간 가족과 떨어져 지낸 그의 귀환은 실종 이후 생사를 알지 못했던 가족과 마을 주민들에게 큰 감격을 안겼다.

루메 마을 책임자 킴비 초보는 “가족들이 그녀를 다시 만날 수 없을 것이라고 생각할 정도로 오랜 시간 고통을 겪었다”고 전했다. 가족과 주민들은 그의 생사를 알 수 없는 상황에서 장례 의식까지 치렀던 것으로 알려졌다.

초보는 “그가 살아서 돌아온 것은 가족과 공동체 전체에 깊은 감동을 주는 일”이라며 “오랜 세월이 지난 뒤 살아 돌아온 것에 하나님께 감사한다”고 말했다.

르웬조리 지역 책임자 카세레카 마파티 자페트도 이번 납치를 규탄하며 “무장단체의 민간인 납치는 용납할 수 없는 행위”라고 밝혔다. 무투왕가 지역 교회 지도자들도 “다르케의 귀환을 환영한다”며 “여전히 무장단체에 억류돼 있는 다른 사람들을 잊지 말아야 한다”고 강조했다.

국제앰네스티는 2026년 5월 발표한 보고서에서 ADF가 민간인을 대상으로 살해와 납치, 강제노동, 아동 모집, 여성과 소녀에 대한 성폭력을 자행했다고 밝혔다.

유엔 인권최고대표사무소도 지난 10월 유엔 인권이사회에 제출한 보고서에서 2026년 1월 1일부터 9월 15일까지 ADF와 관련된 인권침해 319건을 확인했으며, 피해자는 1,500명 이상이라고 밝혔다.

다르케의 구출은 장기간 실종 상태였던 한 기독교 여성이 가족과 공동체로 돌아왔다는 점에서 의미가 있다. 그러나 동부 콩고에서는 여전히 무장단체의 공격과 납치로 가족과 떨어져 지내는 주민들이 남아 있다. ICC는 다르케의 회복과 함께 아직 억류된 사람들의 안전과 귀환을 위해 기도해 줄 것을 요청했다.

一名基督教女性在刚果民主共和国东部被与伊斯兰国（IS）有关联的武装组织绑架并关押了4年多，后被乌干达军队解救。她作证说，在被关押期间，她曾遭受性暴力，并被强迫皈依伊斯兰教，但她坚守了内心的信仰。据《基督教日报国际版》（CDI）报道，国际基督教迫害监测组织（ICC）在最近发布的一份报告中表示：“2022年7月在刚果民主共和国东部卢梅村被绑架的卡通古·姆巴卡·达尔克（Katungu Mbaka Darke）在伊图里省被乌干达人民国防军（UPDF）解救。” 当时，在晚上9点左右，民主同盟军（ADF）的成员袭击了该村庄，达尔克在这一过程中被绑架。ADF是一个在刚果民主共和国东部活动的武装组织，与伊斯兰国（IS）有联系。

达尔克在被拘禁期间遭受了性暴力和宗教胁迫。他在向国际刑事法院（ICC）作证时表示：“我被绑架时还很小。他们中的一个人强迫我发生性关系。他们还强迫我皈依伊斯兰教，背诵古兰经的经文。表面上我接受了，但心里知道耶稣就是神。” 据称，她在被拘禁期间与一名ADF成员生下了两个孩子。她长期与家人分离后终于归来，令自她失踪后一直不知其生死下落的家人和村民深受感动。鲁梅村负责人金比·乔博（Kimbi Chobo）表示：“她的家人承受了很长时间的痛苦，以至于他们以为再也见不到她了。” 据了解，在无法得知她生死的情况下，家人和村民甚至为她举行了葬礼。

楚波表示：“他活着回来，对他的家人和整个社区来说都是一件令人深受感动的事情。”他还说：“感谢上帝，在这么多年之后，他还能活着回来。” 鲁文佐里地区负责人卡塞雷卡·马帕蒂·扎佩特（Kasereka Mapati Japhet）也谴责了此次绑架事件，并表示“武装团体绑架平民是不可容忍的行为”。穆图旺加地区的教会领袖们也表示：“我们欢迎达尔克归来”，并强调：“我们不应忘记那些仍被武装组织关押的人。” 国际特赦组织在2026年5月发布的一份报告中指出，ADF对平民实施了杀害、绑架、强迫劳动、招募儿童兵以及对妇女和女童的性暴力。

联合国人权事务高级专员办事处在去年10月提交给联合国人权理事会的报告中也指出，2026年1月1日至9月15日期间，共确认了319起与ADF有关的侵犯人权事件，受害者超过1500人。达尔克的获救具有重要意义，因为这名长期失踪的基督徒女性得以重返家人和社区。然而，在刚果东部，仍有居民因武装团体的袭击和绑架而与家人分离。ICC呼吁大家为达尔克的康复以及仍被关押的人的安全和回归祈祷。

articles.summary_zh: 下一代的灵性复兴与青年领袖培养，11月24日至26日在军中宣教场所猛虎教会举办的活动，超越福音复兴，关注青年宣教领袖。韩国教会正面临下一代人数减少和青年人远离教会的挑战，因此将以军中宣教场所为中心，举办一次营会，探索青年福音化的新可能性。Daseum愿景宣教团（代表韩亚岚牧师）将于11月24日（周二）至26日（周四）在京畿道加平的首都机械化步兵师猛虎教会举办为期3天2夜的“第20届Daseum MMB营会（Military Mission Bridge Camp）”。本次营会由首都机械化步兵师基督教军牧部主办，Daseum愿景宣教会社承办，以“Back to the Gospel：回归福音”为主题，围绕罗马书1章16-17节的经文展开。值此第20届之际，本次营会不仅是一次简单的军人信仰培训会，更是为韩国教会的未来承担责任的活动。
articles.title_zh: “回归福音！”第20届多世友MMB营会
articles.content:
다음 세대 영적 회복과 청년 리더십 양성, 군선교 현장에서 11월 24-26일 맹호교회에서 복음 회복 넘어 청년선교 리더십

한국교회가 다음 세대 감소와 청년층 교회 이탈이라는 과제에 직면한 가운데, 군선교 현장을 중심으로 청년 복음화의 새로운 가능성을 모색하는 캠프가 열린다.

다세움비전선교회(대표 한아람 목사)는 오는 11월 24일(화)부터 26일(목)까지 2박 3일간 경기 가평에 위치한 수도기계화보병사단 맹호교회에서 ‘제20회 다세움 MMB캠프(Military Mission Bridge Camp)’를 개최한다.

이번 캠프는 수도기계화보병사단 기독군종부가 주최하고 다세움비전선교회가 주관하며, ‘Back to the Gospel: 다시 복음으로’라는 주제 아래 로마서 1장 16-17절 말씀을 중심으로 진행된다.

이번 캠프는 20회를 맞아 단순한 군 장병 신앙수련회를 넘어, 한국교회의 미래를 책임질 청년세대의 영적 정체성을 회복하고 복음의 사명을 가진 청년 리더십을 세우는 데 목적을 두고 있다.

제20회 다세움MMB캠프는 수도기계화보병사단 기독교 신우들을 대상으로 진행되며, 지역교회와 성도들의 후원 및 협력으로 준비되고 있다.

한국교회 청년복음화 위기, 군선교 현장에서

오늘날 한국교회는 다음 세대 신앙 계승과 청년 복음화라는 중요한 과제를 안고 있다. 급변하는 사회문화적 환경과 가치관 변화 속에 청년 세대와 교회 사이 거리는 점차 멀어지고 있으며, 기존 교회 중심적 전도 방식만으로는 새로운 세대에 복음을 효과적으로 전달하는 데 한계가 있다는 목소리가 커지고 있다.

이러한 상황에서 군선교 현장은 한국교회가 다시 주목해야 할 중요한 선교적 접촉점으로 평가받고 있다.

군 복무 기간은 청년들이 익숙한 일상에서 벗어나 자신의 삶과 미래, 존재의 의미를 깊이 고민하는 시기다. 동시에 다양한 지역과 환경에서 성장한 청년들이 한자리에 모이는 특별한 공동체이기도 하다.

다세움비전선교회는 바로 이 지점에 주목해 왔다. 군 복무 중 복음을 접한 청년들이 단순히 군 생활 동안 신앙생활을 경험하는 데 그치지 않고, 전역 후에도 지역교회와 연결해 지속적으로 신앙을 성장시키고, 또 다른 청년에게 복음을 전하는 선교적 리더로 세워지는 것이 핵심이다.

이는 군선교를 일회성 전도행사나 종교활동 차원에서 바라보는 것이 아니라, ‘복음전도– 제자훈련– 청년리더십 양성– 지역교회 연결– 선교적 재생산’으로 이어지는 지속 가능한 청년복음화 전략으로 확장하는 것이다.

제20회 다세움MMB캠프, 복음의 본질로 돌아가는 2박 3일

이번 캠프는 ‘Back to the Gospel’이라는 주제에 걸맞게 복음의 본질을 다시 발견하고, 복음이 청년들의 삶과 가치관을 변화시키는 실제 능력이 되도록 프로그램을 구성했다.

첫날에는 개회예배를 시작으로 찬양콘서트와 특별강연, 청년리더십 팀빌딩, 저녁찬양집회가 이어진다.

둘째 날에는 신앙과 삶을 연결하는 다양한 특강과 간증, 청년리더십 양성 프로젝트 MMB비전토크, 저녁찬양집회와 기도회를 통해 개인의 신앙적 결단과 공동체적 사명을 구체화한다.

마지막 날에는 군선교 비전과 사명을 공유하고, 참가 장병들이 직접 작성한 소감문을 발표하며, 군 복무 이후에도 복음의 사명을 이어갈 수 있도록 도전하는 시간을 갖는다.

특히 이번 캠프에는 군종목사와 군선교 사역자, 목회자, 기독교 문화사역자, CCM 아티스트 등 다양한 분야의 사역자들이 함께 참여한다.

번개탄TV, 테바워십을 비롯한 여러 찬양 및 문화사역팀도 협력하여 청년세대의 눈높이에 맞춘 복음적 소통과 예배의 장을 마련할 예정이다.

군선교 새 패러다임, 전역 후까지 책임지는 복음의 연결

다세움 MMB캠프가 강조하는 가장 중요한 가치는 ‘연결’이다. 군선교의 열매가 군 복무 기간에만 머물지 않고, 전역 이후 지역교회로 이어져야 한다는 것이다.

그동안 군선교는 많은 장병에게 복음을 전하고 신앙의 첫걸음을 내딛게 하는 중요한 역할을 감당해 왔다. 그러나 전역 이후 신앙공동체와 연결되지 못하거나 교회 정착에 어려움을 겪는 청년들에 대한 지속적인 관심과 체계적 지원 역시 중요한 과제로 남아 있다.

다세움비전선교회는 이러한 현실을 극복하기 위해 군부대와 지역교회, 청년사역 공동체를 연결하는 선교적 플랫폼을 지향하고 있다.

특히 MMB캠프를 통해 복음의 정체성을 발견한 장병들이 군 생활 속에서 신앙의 영향력을 발휘하고, 전역 후에는 지역교회와 사회 속에서 복음의 증인으로 살아갈 수 있도록 청년리더십 양성에 힘쓰고 있다.

이는 단순히 군선교의 외형적 성장을 추구하는 것이 아니라, 한 사람의 청년이 복음 안에서 변화되고 또 다른 청년을 세우는 선순환 구조를 만드는 데 초점을 맞춘다.

한 명의 장병이 변화되면 한 공동체가 변화될 수 있고, 한 명의 청년리더가 세워지면 또 다른 다음세대를 세우는 복음의 통로가 될 수 있다는 믿음이다.

“다음 세대 살아야 전 세대가 산다”

다세움비전선교회는 ‘다음 세대가 살아야 전 세대가 산다’는 비전 아래, 군선교와 청년복음화 사역을 이어오고 있다.

한아람 대표목사는 이번 캠프를 준비하며 한국교회가 군선교를 바라보는 시각의 전환이 필요하다고 강조했다.

한 목사는 “군선교는 단순히 군 장병들에게 복음을 전하는 사역을 넘어 한국교회의 미래를 준비하는 중요한 청년선교 현장”이라며 “군대에서 만나는 한 명의 청년이 복음으로 변화되고, 전역 후 지역교회에 정착하여 또 다른 청년을 세워간다면 그것이야말로 한국교회 청년복음화의 실질적인 대안이 될 수 있다”고 전했다.

이어 “오늘날 한국교회가 다음 세대를 걱정하는 데 머물 것이 아니라, 다음 세대가 실제로 살아나는 현장에 함께 투자하고 동역해야 한다”며 “군선교 현장에서 시작된 복음의 불씨가 지역교회와 대학, 직장과 사회로 확산되기를 소망한다”고 밝혔다.

또 “이번 캠프가 단순한 행사로 끝나는 것이 아니라, 청년들이 다시 복음으로 돌아가 자신의 삶을 하나님께 드리고, 복음의 사명을 품은 새로운 세대의 리더로 일어서는 전환점이 되기를 기대한다”고 덧붙였다.

한국교회 청년 복음화는 특정 교회나 선교단체만의 노력으로 해결하기 어려운 과제다. 군교회와 지역교회, 선교단체와 청년사역 기관이 서로 협력하며 청년들 신앙 여정을 함께 책임지는 연합적 선교구조가 필요하다.

특히 군 복무 중 복음을 경험한 장병들이 전역 후에도 신앙을 지속할 수 있도록 지역교회 정착 지원, 청년 제자훈련, 신앙 멘토링, 선교적 리더십 개발 등 구체적인 후속 양육 체계가 마련돼야 한다.

다세움비전선교회는 앞으로도 MMB캠프를 중심으로 군선교 현장의 복음화와 청년리더십 양성, 전역 장병의 지역교회 연결을 위한 협력체계를 확장해 나갈 계획이다.

제20회 다세움MMB캠프는 이러한 비전을 한국교회와 함께 나누고, 군선교가 청년복음화의 중요한 선교적 대안으로 자리매김할 수 있도록 새로운 가능성을 제시하는 자리가 될 전망이다.

“복음으로 한 청년을 세우고, 그 청년을 통해 또 다른 세대를 세운다.”

다세움비전선교회가 꿈꾸는 한국교회 청년복음화의 미래다.

下一代的灵性复兴与青年领袖培养，11月24日至26日在军中传道现场的猛虎教会举办“超越福音复兴的青年传道领袖”活动

在韩国教会面临下一代信徒人数减少和青年人离开教会的挑战之际，一场以军中宣教为重点、旨在探索青年福音化新可能性的营会即将举行。Daseum愿景宣教团（代表：韩亚岚牧师）将于11月24日（星期二）至26日（星期四）在位于京畿道加平郡的首都机械化步兵师猛虎教会举办为期3天2夜的“第20届Daseum MMB营会（Military Mission Bridge Camp）”。

本次营会由首都机械化步兵师基督教军牧部主办，由达世隅异象宣教会社承办，以“Back to the Gospel：回归福音”为主题，围绕罗马书第1章16-17节的经文展开。本次营会是第20届，其目的不仅在于举办一场简单的军人信仰培训会，更在于帮助将担负起韩国教会未来的年轻一代重拾其属灵身份，并培养肩负福音使命的青年领袖。第20届Daseum MMB营面向首都机械化步兵师的基督徒官兵举办，目前正在地方教会和信徒的支持与合作下筹备。韩国教会青年福音化危机，在军队传道现场

如今，韩国教会面临着将信仰传承给下一代和青年福音化这两项重要任务。

在社会文化环境和价值观急剧变化的背景下，年轻一代与教会之间的距离正日益拉大。越来越多的人认为，仅靠传统的以教会为中心的传福音方式，已无法有效地将福音传达给新一代。在这种情况下，军中传教场所被认为是韩国教会应当重新关注的重要传教接触点。服兵役期间是青年人脱离熟悉日常生活的时期，也是他们深入思考自己的人生、未来和存在意义的时期。与此同时，它也是一个特殊的群体，将来自不同地区和成长环境的青年聚集在一起。Daseum愿景宣教会社一直关注这一点。

关键在于，在服兵役期间接触到福音的青年人不仅要在军旅生涯中经历信仰生活，而且在退伍后也要与当地教会建立联系，持续成长信仰，并成为向其他青年人传播福音的宣教领袖。这不是将军队宣教视为一次性的传福音活动或宗教活动，而是将其扩展为一项可持续的青年福音化战略，即“传福音—门徒训练—培养青年领袖—与地方教会建立联系—宣教性再生产”。第20届达世友MMB营会：为期2晚3天的回归福音本质之旅

本次营会以“回归福音”为主题，旨在让参与者重新发现福音的本质，并使福音成为一种真正能够改变青年人生活和价值观的力量。

第一天以开幕敬拜仪式开始，随后是赞美音乐会、特别讲座、青年领袖团队建设和晚间赞美会。第二天，通过各种连接信仰与生活的特别讲座和见证、MMB Vision Talk、青年领袖培训项目以及晚间赞美会和祈祷会来体现个人的宗教决定和社区使命。最后一天，将分享军事宣教的愿景和使命，将呈现参与士兵撰写的感言，并有时间挑战他们即使在服完兵役后也能继续传福音的使命。特别是来自各个领域的牧师，包括军事牧师、军事宣教工作者、牧师、基督教文化牧师和CCM艺术家，都参加了这个营。包括Lightning TV和Teva Worship在内的几个赞美和文化事工团队也计划合作，提供一个适合年轻一代需求的福音传播和敬拜场所。

军事使命的新范式，一种福音联系，在退役后承担责任。

Daseum MMB Camp 强调的最重要的价值是“连接”。军事宣教的成果不应仅在服兵役期间保留，而应在退伍后继续留在当地教会。与此同时，军事宣教在向许多士兵传播福音并帮助他们迈出信仰的第一步方面发挥了重要作用。然而，对退伍后无法与信仰团体建立联系或难以在教堂安顿下来的年轻人持续的关注和系统的支持也仍然是重要的任务。为了克服这一现实，Daseum Vision Mission 旨在成为一个连接军事基地、当地教会和青年事工社区的传教平台。

特别是，我们致力于培养青年领袖，让通过MMB营发现自己福音身份的士兵在服兵役期间发挥信仰的影响力，并在退伍后在当地教会和社会中成为福音的见证人。这并不是单纯追求军事宣教的外在成长，而是着眼于创造一个良性循环，一个年轻人在福音中被改变，又造就另一个年轻人。人们相信，当一名士兵发生改变时，一个社区就能发生改变；当一名年轻的领袖被确立时，它就能成为建设下一代的福音渠道。 “下一代人必须活着，这样上一代人才能生存。”

Daseum Vision Mission一直以“下一代必须生存，以便所有世代都能生存”为愿景，开展军事宣教和青少年福传工作。

在准备本次训练营时，首席执行官 Aram Han 强调韩国教会需要改变对军事宣教的看法。韩牧师说：“军事宣教是一个重要的青年宣教领域，它为韩国教会的未来做好准备，而不仅仅是向军人传福音。如果我们在军队中遇到的年轻人被福音改变，退伍后定居在当地教会，并养育其他年轻人，那么这可以成为韩国教会青少年福传的真正替代方案。”他接着说：“今天的韩国教会不应该只关心下一代，而应该在下一代实际生存的领域进行投资和共同努力”，并补充说，“我希望从军事宣教领域开始的福音火花能够蔓延到地方教会、大学、工作场所和社会。”

他补充说：“我们希望本次营会不是一次简单的活动，而是成为年轻人回归福音、将生命献给神、成为拥抱福音使命的新一代领袖的转折点。”韩国教会的青少年福传是一项仅靠特定教会或宣教组织的努力才能解决的艰巨任务。需要一个统一的宣教结构，军事教会、地方教会、宣教组织和青年事工组织相互合作，为年轻人的信仰之旅负责。特别是要建立具体的后续培育体系，如支持入驻当地教会、青少年门徒培训、信仰辅导、宣教领袖培养等，让在服兵役期间经历福音的士兵在退伍后能够继续信仰。

Daseum Vision Mission 计划继续扩大其合作系统，以 MMB 营地为重点，向军事宣教地点传福音，培养青年领导力，并将士兵与当地教会联系起来。第20届Daseum MMB营预计将成为与韩国教会分享这一愿景的机会，并提供新的可能性，以便军事宣教能够成为青年福传的重要传教替代方案。 “我们通过福音培养了一个年轻人，通过那个年轻人，我们又培养了另一代人。”

这就是Daseum Vision Missionary Society所梦想的韩国教会青少年福传的未来。

articles.content: A group of men who assaulted two Christian girls for attempting to convert Hindus to Christianity in Telangana, India, has sparked outrage throughout India. A video of the incident, which became public in early November, has raised concerns over Hindu nationalists taking the law into their hands and attacking Christians over allegations of conversion. The incident took place around two months ago in Almasguda, Maheshwaram mandal, under the Meerpet police station limits in Rangareddy district of Telangana state near Hyderabad, the capital city. Two of the attackers have been identified and arrested by the police after protests by the Christian community in front of the police station. Accusations and Assault In the video, a group of men is seen confronting the two young women — who appeared to be minors — accusing them of attempting to convert school children to Christianity by offering them chocolates. The two girls are heard denying the allegations, saying they were merely visiting relatives in the area. However, one of the men slaps them brutally and verbally abuses them in public. One woman is seen sitting nearby, but she does not make any attempt to stop the men from attacking the girls. While the girls’ agonized apologies are heard, the man is relentlessly hitting the two girls alternately without mercy, even as another man is making half-hearted attempts to restrain the attacker. One of the girls has her glasses shattered by a forceful blow to her face from the man, who is not done hitting before he assaults the other pleading girl. The attackers accused the young women of attempting forced religious conversions by allegedly distributing chocolates to schoolchildren — a frequent, unsubstantiated trope used by Hindu nationalists in India to justify street-level violence. Protests and Public Response Meanwhile, the video of the assault went viral, triggering immediate street protests by members of the Dalit Christian organizations on Nov. 4 to demand the arrest of the perpetrators. Dalit Christians (or Christian Dalits) are people in the Indian subcontinent who converted to Christianity from historically marginalized, low-caste or “untouchable” (Dalit) backgrounds. The protests by the Dalit Christians were met with aggressive counter-sloganeering by local Hindu outfits, forcing the Telangana state police to deploy additional forces and use force to prevent a full-scale riot. While the police swiftly arrested the primary perpetrators, the incident underscored a deeper systemic shift: the normalization of extrajudicial moral policing. Christian leaders, political figures and human rights advocates condemned the assault and called for an impartial investigation and protection. Sabitha Indra Reddy, former Telangana minister, condemned the brutality on X. Reddy stated that objections regarding religious freedom should be pursued legally rather than through violence against women. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . 一群人因试图在印度特拉干纳将印度教皈依基督教而袭击了两名基督教女孩,这引起了整个印度的愤怒。 11月初公开的一则事件视频引起了印度民族主义者对印度教徒掌握法律并攻击基督教徒指控皈依的关注.

事件发生在两个月前,在首都海得拉巴附近的Telangana州Rangareddy区的Meheshwaram mandal的Almasguda, 两名袭击者在警察局门口基督教社区抗议后被警方指认并逮捕.

指控和攻击 在影片中,一群男子面对两名年轻女子——她们似乎是未成年人——指责他们试图通过提供巧克力来使在校儿童皈依基督教. 听到两名女孩否认这些指控,说她们只是去探访该地区的亲属。

然而,其中一人在公开场合粗暴地殴打他们并辱骂他们。 一名妇女被看见坐在附近,但没有试图阻止男子攻击女孩。 这名男子毫不留情地不择手段地殴打两名女孩,

其中一个女孩的眼镜被那个男人猛烈地打到她脸上打得粉碎了,而那个男人在攻击另一个恳求的女孩之前没有打完。 袭击者指责青年妇女试图强迫改变宗教信仰,据称他们向学童分发巧克力——印度印度民族主义者经常用来为街头暴力辩护,但没有根据。

同时,袭击的视频也传入了病毒,引发了达利特基督教组织成员于11月4日立即上街抗议,要求逮捕肇事者。 贱民基督徒(或称基督教贱民)是印度次大陆上从历史上被边缘化、低种姓或“不可接触”(达利特)背景皈依基督教的人。

达利特基督徒的抗议活动遭遇了当地印度教服饰的猛烈反攻,迫使泰兰加纳州警方增派了部队并使用武力来防止全面骚乱. 虽然警方迅速逮捕了主要肇事者,但这一事件突出表明了更深刻的系统转变:法外道德警察的正常化。

基督教领袖、政治人物和人权倡导者谴责这次袭击,并呼吁进行公正的调查和保护。 前特兰加纳部长萨比莎·因德拉·雷迪(Sabitha Indra Reddy)谴责了对X的残暴行为. 雷迪表示,对宗教自由的反对应该通过法律手段而不是通过对妇女的暴力行为来进行. 更多新闻报导,

articles.title_zh: 埃及基督徒在利比亚殉道
articles.content: In early October, a 20-year-old Coptic Christian was kidnapped and killed at the hands of the Islamic State group. Milad Malak lived in Sebarbay, Egypt, and served as a church deacon at a local Coptic church. However, because of the country’s economic decline, he traveled to Libya on Sept. 2 to find work. He made a day’s journey with two Muslim friends and arrived in Zliten, where they stayed with other Egyptian migrant workers. On the morning of Oct. 4, ISIS militants kidnapped them. The captors subjected the group to abuse while they held them hostage for ransom money. Milad’s friends were released after their families paid a $4,700 ransom. They are now receiving medical treatment at a hospital in Egypt. Milad’s sister, Madonna Malek, told Worthy News that their family paid a ransom, but because he was the only Christian in the group, his kidnappers refused to release him and violently pressured him to convert to Islam. Milad stood strong in his faith until the end. He told his persecutors, “Even if you cut me into pieces, I would never renounce my faith.” When the militants realized they could not force him to abandon his God, they killed him. Faithful Until the End After hearing about his death from his friends, Milad’s family appealed to the Egyptian government, asking them to intervene and demand that his body be returned home. Several weeks went by until it was finally released, and on Oct. 28, grieving family members and fellow Christians gathered to celebrate the life of their beloved son and friend. “He was faithful to Christ till his last breath,” a family friend said. Open Doors ranked Libya as the ninth most dangerous place to be a Christian. A Muslim-majority nation, Christians face heavy pressure to abandon their faith. Milad’s death has reminded believers of the massacre that occurred in 2015, when 20 Coptic Christians and one Ghanaian were beheaded by militants in Libya for standing strong in their faith. Milad joins them as yet another martyr who inspires Christians worldwide to be bold witnesses for Christ until the very end. Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . 10月初,一名20岁的科普特·克里斯蒂安被伊斯兰国集团绑架并杀害. 米拉德·马拉克居住在埃及塞巴拜,并在当地的科普特教堂担任教堂执事. 然而,由于该国经济下滑,他于9月2日前往利比亚寻找工作。

他与两个穆斯林朋友共度了一天的旅程,并抵达兹利滕,在那里他们与其他埃及移徙工人住在一起。 10月4日上午,伊斯兰国武装分子绑架了他们。 抓捕者在以赎金为人质时虐待该团伙。 Mirad的朋友在家人支付了4700美元的赎金后被释放。

他们目前正在埃及的一家医院接受治疗。 米拉德的妹妹麦当娜·马利克(Madonna Malek)告诉沃西新闻,他们的家人支付了赎金,但由于他是这群人中唯一的基督徒,绑匪拒绝释放他,并用暴力逼迫他皈依伊斯兰教. 米拉德坚守信仰,直到最后.

他对他的迫害者说:即使你把我割成碎片,我也不会放弃我的信仰。 当激进分子意识到他们不能强迫他放弃上帝时,他们杀了他. Milad的家人在从朋友那里得知他的死讯后,

几个星期过去了,直到最终发行,10月28日,悲痛的家人和基督徒同胞聚集在一起,庆祝他们心爱的儿子和朋友的生命. 一位家庭朋友说:“他忠于基督直到最后一口气”。 开放门将利比亚列为第九个最危险的基督徒地点.

作为一个穆斯林占多数的民族,基督徒面临着放弃信仰的沉重压力. Milad的死让信徒想起了2015年发生的大屠杀,当时利比亚有20名科普特基督徒和1名加纳人因坚守信仰而被激进分子斩首. 米拉德与他们一起成为另一个烈士,他激励全世界的基督徒成为基督的大胆见证,直到最后.

articles.content: By ICC Fellow Lisa Navarrette For years, Fadi has told his children the same thing: We stay. He is a Christian father in Lebanon. His family has lived in the same town for generations, and his parents are buried nearby. Fadi’s children were baptized in the church where he married his wife, Nour. His small business survived political unrest, the economic collapse, the Beirut port explosion, and another round of regional conflict. Leaving always felt like surrender. But lately, the calculation has changed. Fuel costs have risen again. Groceries take a larger share of the family’s income. Electricity is unreliable, so the business depends partly on a generator. Transportation costs more. His oldest daughter has been accepted to a university abroad, while his younger son talks openly about finding work in Europe. One evening, Fadi places two folders on the kitchen table. One contains bills. The other contains immigration documents. “We don’t have to decide tonight,” she said. Fadi looks at the paperwork for a long time. Years earlier, violence made the family afraid to leave home. Now economics is making them wonder whether they should leave the country. That is the final link in the chain this series examines. Fighting to Stay High fuel prices do not create religious persecution. But when families have already endured violence, displacement, discrimination, destroyed livelihoods, or political instability, rising energy costs can make recovery harder and staying less sustainable. In 2026, the World Bank warned that the Middle East conflict had created a major energy shock, raising fuel prices, increasing inflation, disrupting transportation and logistics, and weakening economic growth. Its October 2026 regional economic update found that fragile and conflict-affected economies were experiencing especially severe pressure , with poverty still rising in parts of the region even as it declined elsewhere. Those regional trends eventually become household questions: Can the business stay open? Can the family still afford food? Will there be jobs for the children? Is rebuilding worth the cost? Lebanon illustrates how those pressures can accumulate. Christians there have not experienced the same mass expulsion seen in parts of Iraq or Syria, but International Christian Concern (ICC) has documented how economic collapse, political instability, regional conflict, and emigration continue to weaken one of the Middle East’s most important Christian communities. No single crisis explains why a family leaves. That is what makes the process easy to overlook. A Christian family may survive violence but lose its savings. It may survive political instability but lose its business. It may rebuild after displacement only to discover that electricity, fuel, food, and transportation have become increasingly expensive. Eventually, the question is no longer only whether the family is safe. It is whether the family can build a future. Affording Daily Life The same dynamic is evident in Syria, where many people have tried to return after years of war. In May 2026, ICC reported that about 1.67 million refugees and 1.9 million internally displaced Syrians had returned since December 2024. Yet the agency warned that damaged housing, limited livelihoods, weak infrastructure, poverty, and restricted access to basic services continued to threaten the sustainability of those returns. A separate 2026 assessment hosted by UNHCR reached a similar conclusion : whether people remain after returning depends heavily on housing, employment, services, and economic opportunity. For Christian communities, that distinction matters. Imagine a family returning to a Syrian town after years abroad. They repair part of their home. Their children reenter school. 他的小企业在政治动荡,经济崩溃,贝鲁特港口爆炸以及另一轮区域冲突中幸存下来. 离开总是觉得投降。 但最近,计算方式发生了变化。 燃料成本再次上升。 食谱占家庭收入的较大份额。 电力不可靠,因此业务部分依赖于发电机. 运输成本更高。

他的大女儿被录取到国外的一所大学,而小儿子则公开谈论在欧洲找工作. 一天晚上,法迪把两个文件夹放在厨房桌子上. 一个有账单。 另一个文件载有移民证件。 “我们不必在今晚决定, 法迪很长一段时间都在看文件 几年前,暴力使家庭不敢离家。

现在经济学让他们怀疑他们是否应该出国。 这是本系列审查的链条的最后环节。 高油价斗争不会造成宗教迫害。

但是,当家庭已经忍受了暴力、流离失所、歧视、生计被摧毁或政治不稳定时,能源成本的上升会使恢复更加困难,并降低可持续性。

2026年,世界银行警告说,中东冲突造成了严重的能源冲击,燃料价格上涨,通货膨胀加剧,交通和后勤中断,经济增长减弱.

其2026年10月的区域经济最新情况发现,脆弱和受冲突影响的经济体正承受着特别严重的压力,该区域部分地区的贫困现象仍在加剧,尽管其他地区的贫困状况有所下降。 这些区域趋势最终成为家庭问题:企业能否继续开放? 家人还能买得起食物吗? 孩子们会有工作吗?

重建值得付出代价吗? 黎巴嫩说明了这些压力如何能够累积。 但国际基督教关注组织(ICC)记录了经济崩溃、政治不稳定、地区冲突和移民继续削弱中东最重要的基督教社区之一。

没有一个危机能解释一个家庭为什么离开。 这使得这一进程容易被忽视。 一个基督教家庭可能会在暴力中幸存下来,但却会失去积蓄。 它可能在政治不稳定的情况下生存下来,但失去了业务。 它可能在流离失所后重建,只为了发现电力、燃料、粮食和交通越来越昂贵。

最后,问题不再仅仅是家庭是否安全。 家庭是否能够建立未来。 每日生活 同样的动态在叙利亚也很明显,许多人在多年战争之后试图返回叙利亚。 2026年5月,国际刑事法院报告说,自2024年12月以来,约有167万难民和190万境内流离失所的叙利亚人返回。

然而,该机构警告说,住房受损、生计有限、基础设施薄弱、贫穷以及获得基本服务的机会有限,继续威胁着这些回返的可持续性。 难民署主办的2026年的单独评估得出了类似结论:人们返回后是否仍留在当地,在很大程度上取决于住房、就业、服务和经济机会。

对基督教社区来说,这种区别很重要。 想象一个家庭在海外多年后返回叙利亚城镇。 他们修补了一部分家 他们的孩子重新入学。 父亲开始重建小生意. 然后费用开始增加。 电力仍然不可靠。 发电机的燃料成本更高。 工作和上学的交通占收入的较大份额。

articles.content: Presunto delincuente, herido en el abdomen Un hombre resultó herido de un disparo en el abdomen durante un procedimiento policial realizado este mediodía en Villa Santillán. Según pudo reconstruir LA ARENA,luego de que efectivos policiales fueran alertados por vecinos sobre la presencia de una persona que saltaba por los techos e ingresaba a los patios de distintas viviendas, se produjo una persecución, y ante reiteradas voces de alto de los efectivos que lo perseguían, el sospechoso habría sacado algo de su cintura, por lo que uno de los policías le disparó. A pesar de la herida, el hombre siguió la marcha y se escondió en su propia casa. A los pocos minutos, el personal policial llegó a detenerlo y algunos familiares intentaron impedirlo. Finalmente, el herido fue asistido por una ambulancia del SEM, y fue trasladado al Hospital Favaloro, donde quedó internado, fuera de peligro. Llamados al 101. Según pudo saber este diario, alrededor de las 11.30 comenzaron a recibirse llamados al servicio de emergencias 101. Algunos vecinos señalaron que el sospechoso era un hombre conocido en el ambiente delictivo, residente del mismo barrio. De acuerdo con los testimonios recogidos, también habría ingresado a patios de viviendas y sería habitual que circule armado, ya sea con arma de fuego o con armas blancas.Cuando llegó el personal policial, los efectivos comenzaron a recorrer el sector y buscar al sospechoso por los patios y los techos, hasta que finalmente lo encontraron en la vía pública. En ese momento, le dieron reiteradas voces de alto, le ordenaron que se detuviera y se arrojara al suelo. Sin embargo, siempre de acuerdo con la reconstrucción preliminar del episodio, el hombre habría desobedecido las indicaciones y amenazado a los policías con dispararles. Los efectivos advirtieron que llevaba un objeto en la cintura que parecía ser un arma de fuego. Amenaza. En medio de la persecución, el hombre habría llevado la mano hacia ese objeto y, ante lo que interpretó como una amenaza inminente, uno de los policías efectuó un disparo con su arma reglamentaria, que impactó en el abdomen del sospechoso. A pesar de la herida, el hombre continuó corriendo hasta ingresar a su vivienda.Una vez en el lugar, se convocó a una ambulancia. Sin embargo, familiares del herido habrían impedido inicialmente que el personal policial lo asistiera. Finalmente, fue trasladado al Hospital Favaloro, donde recibió atención médica. La lesión no requirió una intervención quirúrgica y, según la información conocida por este diario, se encuentra fuera de peligro. Investigación en marcha. Tras el episodio se desplegaron las actuaciones correspondientes, con peritajes y distintas medidas para reconstruir las circunstancias en las que se produjo el disparo. La investigación se encuentra en manos del Ministerio Público Fiscal, representado por Cristian Casais y Selva Paggi. También tomó intervención la Fiscalía de Investigaciones Administrativas, dado que se trata de un hecho en el que un efectivo policial utilizó su arma reglamentaria. Versión policial. El Ministerio de Seguridad y Justicia y la Jefatura de Policía emitieron un comunicado conjunto informando sobre el incidente. Afirmaron que la intervención inició a raíz de reiterados llamados al 101, por la presencia de una persona que caminaba por los techos. “Quienes realizaron los avisos también aportaron referencias sobre posibles antecedentes de conductas violentas del individuo”, dijeron. Agregaron que continúan desarrollándose las diligencias para esclarecer las circunstancias en que se produjo el incidente. Respecto al efectivo policial que habría realizado el disparo, señalaron que “recibió acompañamiento de personal especializado para el seguimiento psicosocial correspondiente. Asimismo, se iniciaron las actuaciones administrativas pertinentes, con intervención de la Fiscalía de Investigaciones Administrativas”. Por último, confirmaron que el herido recibió atención médica en el Hospital Favaloro. Artícu

articles.summary_zh: 教宗方济各于本周一（9日）在阿根廷的倒数第二次公开活动中，在圣米格尔宫与来自不同基督教社群和宗教传统的代表举行了会晤。
articles.title_zh: 利奥十四世捍卫宗教间对话，视其为人类尊严的守护者——梵蒂冈
articles.content: Em seu penúltimo compromisso público desta segunda-feira (9) na Argentina, o papa Leão XIV liderou um encontro com representantes de diversas comunidades cristãs e tradições religiosas no Palácio San Martín, em Buenos Aires. Em seu pronunciamento no Palácio San Martín, o pontífice americano homenageou seu antecessor, o papa Francisco, e destacou que o evento se realizou "nos pilares do diálogo e da amizade", elementos descritos como "fundamentais" na trajetória do antigo chefe da Igreja Católica. "Nosso encontro, de fato, se assenta nos pilares do diálogo e da amizade, que foram fundamentais na vida do Papa Francisco e que agora desejamos fortalecer, construindo novas pontes e novos caminhos de colaboração na sociedade em que vivemos", afirmou. Robert Francis Prevost ressaltou que a identidade nacional argentina "evoluiu como um caldeirão de diversas etnias, culturas e religiões, formada por povos originários e imigrantes de várias partes do mundo, que trouxeram consigo seus sonhos e sua fé: a princípio, católicos, evangélicos e judeus, e posteriormente muitos outros". "Todos eles, em sua diversidade, aprenderam a trabalhar juntos, a formar famílias e comunidades e a construir cidades em admirável simbiose com as tradições locais. Uniram a nação e perseguiram projetos comuns sem que as religiões jamais fossem fonte de divisão, mas sim ponto de convergência e compromisso compartilhado com a sociedade", observou. O pontífice estruturou sua reflexão a partir de três pilares centrais que emergem da oração sincera: "as religiões como guardiãs da dignidade humana, como expressões de nossa liberdade e como espaços para cultivar a esperança". "As religiões nos lembram que não somos feitos apenas de matéria: nossa carne contém um excedente de vida e significado. Esse mesmo desejo, que se transforma em grito e súplica, atesta que não viemos do nada e não fomos feitos para a morte. Dessa forma, as religiões salvaguardam a dignidade humana. Portanto, cada vez que orarmos, devemos cuidar daqueles que vivem ao nosso redor, traduzindo nossas palavras em fraternidade renovada", analisou. Ao fazer um apelo pela preservação ambiental e moral, Leão XIV exortou os líderes a defender o planeta: "Não destruamos com nossas próprias mãos o 'jardim' que o Criador nos confiou". O papa enfatizou ainda que a fé atua na construção da sociedade ao "educar as consciências e nos libertar dos ídolos", funcionando como um elo vivo entre gerações. "A própria palavra religião é eloquente a esse respeito: refere-se a religare, isto é, conectar, unir as pessoas. Essa relação sustenta nossa jornada através da história. Ao louvarmos a Deus pelo dom da esperança, devemos compartilhá-la com aqueles que sofrem na pobreza, que perderam o sentido da vida e com aqueles que desejam se comprometer com a renovação do mundo segundo a justiça", declarou. Ao encerrar o evento, Leão XIV recitou a oração deixada por Francisco "que compromete todos a fazer o bem". Após acender uma vela entregue por uma criança, o pontífice e as autoridades presentes observaram um minuto de silêncio em favor da paz mundial. TODOS OS DIREITOS RESERVADOS © Copyright ANSA

articles.content: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país desde Juan Pablo II en 1987. En ese marco, la primera actividad del Sumo Pontífice fue un discurso en el Palacio Libertad de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (CABA), frente al presidente de la Nación, Javier Milei. Y aunque sus palabras lógicamente estuvieron apuntadas hacia toda la sociedad, hubo numerosos pasajes que encontraron especial sintonía con el mundo agropecuario. Esto, en la previa de la reunión que León XIV mantendrá el lunes con representantes empresariales, sindicales y de organizaciones sociales, entre los que estarán los presidentes de las cuatro entidades de la Mesa de Enlace. EL PAPA LEÓN XIV EN ARGENTINA Puntualmente, el jefe mayor del Vaticano destacó el valor del esfuerzo cotidiano de los argentinos, con una mención expresa a quienes trabajan en el campo, y reivindicó la importancia de generar oportunidades, estimular la iniciativa privada y aprovechar responsablemente los recursos naturales. “Esta tierra conoce bien el valor del esfuerzo de quienes se ganan la vida en el campo y en las ciudades”, expresó León XIV, al destacar también el papel de los emprendedores y de las familias que sostienen sus hogares a través del trabajo. Asimismo, el Papa reconoció el enorme potencial productivo del país, al señalar que la Argentina cuenta con una extraordinaria riqueza natural, desde sus campos y reservas de agua hasta sus fuentes de energía, minerales y biodiversidad. Así, su mensaje combinó la posibilidad de aprovechar esos recursos para generar desarrollo y bienestar con la responsabilidad de preservar el ambiente y las condiciones de vida de las futuras generaciones. También dedicó un espacio a la innovación, la investigación y las nuevas tecnologías, incluida la inteligencia artificial, destacando su capacidad para transformar la producción y mejorar la vida de las personas. Por otro lado, al expresar una mirada sobre América del Sur, mencionó además a los alimentos, la energía y el conocimiento como elementos que vinculan a los países y abren oportunidades para fortalecer la cooperación regional. LEON XIV, EL MARTÍN FIERO Y EL MATE Asimismo, León XIV ofreció referencias cargadas de simbolismo para la identidad argentina. Por ejemplo, mencionó al Martín Fierro de José Hernández, a Jorge Luis Borges, al tango y a las tradiciones del interior del país. Y no faltó una de las costumbres más arraigadas entre los argentinos: el mate compartido, al que presentó como un gesto cotidiano que favorece la conversación y la cercanía. Por último, hacia el final de su intervención, León XIV evocó a Nuestra Señora de Luján, patrona de la Argentina y figura de especial significado para las comunidades rurales y para generaciones de familias de todo el país. También recordó al papa Francisco, citó a Carlos Gardel y alentó a los argentinos a valorar el patrimonio recibido de las generaciones anteriores y trabajar para dejar un país mejor a quienes vendrán. De esta manera, sin ser un discurso específicamente dirigido al agro, las palabras de León XIV dejaron un reconocimiento al trabajo rural, a la producción, a la iniciativa emprendedora y a las tradiciones que forman parte de la identidad argentina.
